utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the last time before the recess, I wish good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom and I would like to thank all those who support us for the flexibility to enable to us start at 8.30. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you indicated that you'd like to address the Chamber at 8.30. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, thank you very much for having reminded me. What we wanted to point out to you involved two things. Two things and perhaps there will be a third matter later on. But two matters in any event. We wanted to start a 8.30 to allow the Prosecution to develop its position, it might be able to do it. The first point concerns the photograph, the 360-degree photograph, according to the Prosecution's position, according to which something hadn't been calibrated as it should have been, in the so-called GPS procedure, and the statement according to which erroneous figures had been inserted in the device or on occasion were not inserted, as a result we can't rely on the -- we can't consider these photographs to be authentic. And we want to raise this matter. You might modify your decision with regard to each 360-degree photograph because today the Prosecution has provided evidence that the figures are not correct, and as a result, the GPS location is not 100 per cent sure. That's the first matter I wanted to raise. The second matter, Mr. President, is that the Defence knows you have to take many decisions and you have a lot of work. We would simply like to remind you of one matter as far as the second testimony of Dr. Kovacs is concerned, the artillery expert. We have requested that you grant us a delay to present the reasons for which we believe that we could conclude certificate of appeal and could you also provide us with motives which justified the decision to call back Dr. Kovacs, given that we think that the article 94 was violated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The argument of the Defence is quite clear, a mixed decision, that means a decision both explaining the reasons why we allowed the Prosecution to recall the witness and a decision on the admission into evidence of his report, I think it will be delivered today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's only for the sake of the time that we would like to know this, which means, Mr. President, that the seven-day time period would start running as of today, or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider that during the first part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. There are no other matters, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you wanted to address the Court in respect of Mr. Hinchliffe, I would like to indicate that the Chamber has a few more questions for him and then an opportunity will be given to you not on all issues but on a limited number of issues, you may choose yourself, to put additional questions just in order to give the Chamber an impression of what kind of responses we can expect on such type of issues. We don't have to go through the whole report but if you take -- you're perfectly aware, I think of the issues that are of some concern for the Chamber and if you would I would say by a few examples give us an impression on what would be the result of your further examination and we will then perhaps see how this develops. I would think that it should not be -- should not take more than 20 minutes, half an hour perhaps, just by way of example and then we will decide whether we can proceed or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President. Mr. President, just one other matter before we begin the day as proceedings proper, the Prosecution has to consider its position in relation to Zoran Lesic. The situation, as it stands, is that he was always on the witness list, he was always to be recalled, that was made clear at the time that I called him initially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given that the Trial Chamber has rejected the 92 bis statement, the consequence is that we now are obliged to call him to give evidence. Naturally, we will take into account the reasons when we receive them for the decision. I simply point out the obvious that it's the morning of the last day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The statement was rejected late yesterday and we clearly have a -- the timetable difficulty. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. I will inform you in more detail about Mr. Lesic this morning, and as soon as possible. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise but it's one of the things that I was to say at 8.30. We spoke to the representative of the SLO, what we call the SLO, with regard to technical questions. We were asked to inform you of our desires regarding the length of the demand for acquittal. We have a technical problem which I'll present to you very briefly. The Prosecution has structured its dossier, it's taken, for example, 24 cases of sniping and 50 [Realtime transcript read in error "350"] cases of sniping. The Defence's attitude, in order to be logical and consistent with the system that the Prosecution wants, our attitude will be to take each element and to see what may have been proven and what may not, what has not been proven. We can't carry out this exercise with regard to these cases, we can carry it out on ten pages and we have considered with regard to these factual elements that we require about 75 pages, which corresponds, more or less, to 3 pages per incident. If we group them. This is a minimum. Since there will be a certain legal part, and we don't think we can -- we have to do that much work. So our plan will be 75 pages. I see that you have written the figure down. I wanted to indicate it to you, and I thank you for that. There is a mistake in the transcript. But it's not important. Everyone knows that we're talking about 27 cases and five cases and not 350 cases of sniping. Naturally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will inform you today. I can tell you that the number of pages which is ten in the -- in the directions, directives, will give you a larger number of pages, but I'll indicate exactly how many pages later this morning. We have considered the matter already to some extent and of course the new aspect is that we now hear you asking for 75 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin [sic], before we ask the usher to bring in the expert witness, Mr. Hinchliffe, I have one question for you. Has the witness -- have the transcripts of the trial been presented to the -- to Mr. Hinchliffe in respect of the sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript, Mr. President, you addressed me as Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I really need some vacation, just as you all do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's early in the morning on the last day. We provided him with the transcript of the evidence of Ifeta Sahic which relates to incident number 9. That's one of the incidents that on which he made no comment in his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And he will say that he was not take to that incidents. The background is that at that stage we did not have a witness to call. And,. Consequently she gave evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: He's also received two short portions of evidence, one from the evidence of General Karavelic, in respect to the sizes of bullets used by Serbian snipers. And secondly a segment of evidence From Colonel Fraser in relation to shooting of telegraph poles. I should add he was give and number of statements or at least he was given some statements to read on the premises in December, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has he -- have statements been given to him of witnesses that finally were not called?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I've been unable to determine exactly what statements he was given in December. He's made clear to me, as he did yesterday to the Trial Chamber, that all he relied upon for his report were the short accounts given to him by the investigators at each site, a very simple outline of the Prosecution case as to the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In written form available?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, just oral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just oral.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I should stress, as I understand it, it was very brief, and that has been added to by showing him the videos and 360 degree photographs for each incidents. Mr. President, I can also tell you that in proofing him, I have given him again some additional information in relation to each incident, not each incident but some incidents which I will bring out in chief. The evidence of this witness is essentially confined to the technical aspects, in other words, whether the Prosecution case is consistent or inconsistent with his expertise as a sniper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I just add one other thing that might assist you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Hinchliffe is not a professional expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I only know expert witnesses and witnesses, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The only point I seek to make is that I think that the benefit the Trial Chamber will ultimately derive from his evidence is very much that of someone who is an expert in his field and he -- I appreciate your concern about the methodology. At least the way in which that is expressed in his report. I also appreciate it has obvious shortcomings. I think the value of his evidence will become apparent once he goes to the substance of his topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, could you please escort Mr. Hinchliffe into the courtroom? Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I must admit that I haven't really understood what Mr. Ierace was saying, not very well. And in particular, on page 6, line 2, of the transcript, which for me remains to say the least confusing. I don't know what type of -- [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hinchliffe, please be seated may I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you made yesterday? I have a few additional questions for you before your further examination by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hinchliffe, the Chamber is informed that you have read on the premises of the Tribunal some witness statements. Did you make note of which statements you exactly read? Do you have names or dates of these statements? Have you -- did you write them down so that we know exactly what you have read?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. However, I do recognise what I read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Then a few more questions on your report, under 12 reads that the "population had been hunting for centuries, this automatically gave most households, prior to the war, a hunting rifle with telescopic sights and ammunition." Can you tell us what is exactly the source of this observation? And I'm not that much interested in hunting for centuries but especially on the households having hunting rifles with telescopic sights?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is from my experiences when I was working with the UN in 1993 in the region. My experiences with the local population, and my background in intelligence for -- I went there, I conducted an area study.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On what sources?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sources, general background of the country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but what sources? Any books, any historical interviews of people or?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the public books about the actual country, the former Yugoslavia itself. The study was done prior to me deploying in 1993 and assumed I remember and then had experiences later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you couldn't give us a list of books you consulted?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I go further. On serial 2, your reports reads the subunits were clearly ordered to occupy the position. Ordered by whom and on what basis did you make this statement?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I make the statement on the basis having looked at the area and seen the military organised positions there, heights, observations posts and firing positions. It is a standard military layout for a command position with forward positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for that answer. A similar question in serial 6 where you write, "The commander deployed the snipers in this position." I noticed that very often you do not make any mention of commanders or command or whether they were on orders to occupy a certain position. You here again you said, "The commander deployed the sniper in this position." What is the basis of that fact?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a recognised tactic and technique of deploying snipers in this method.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what caused you to put this under 2 and 6 and not in the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to change channels in order to understand what you said, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The mike is on. Sorry, the mike is on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there's either no translation or there is no sound. I see everyone nodding happily so -- perhaps, Mr. Hinchliffe, it's good that the Chamber provides you with a copy of your statement again from the registry. My question is what caused you to write down something about deploying or the commander deployed the snipers in this position on 2 and 6 and not on the other serials?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incident 2 and 6, I felt I could comfortably, in my opinion, assess the situation and give that answer. With others it was less organised and less distinctive, to be a position deployed as.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you have no specific knowledge of a commander --

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's just the technique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear. In serial 20, your report reads, "Very well trained snipers who had been issued precious equipment to engage at will." I'm especially interested in the last part of this sentence. What caused you to write down "to engage at will"?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The precious issuing of equipment for the time and date that this incident happened, being dark hours, the only way that a sniper could see the light source at that distance was to have an image-intensifying night sight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you write down that they had been issued. By whom? Was it already in the possession days before, month before, of the firer?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I am aware is that they had that equipment within their orbits. However, it was quite a specialist piece of equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you write "to engage at will." These last few words, what's the basis of this?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: To engage at will, it was my opinion that for a firer, a sniper to release a shot at night at a likely light source would mean that his rules of engagement were open and therefore if he felt it was a legitimate target or not he could engage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You deduced that from the course of events?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Serial 24, you said that the sniper clearly tracked the tram and chose their own ideal firing position well. What caused you to write down that and not, for example, that they were so lucky that the place they were ordered to go gave an excellent sight or that -- you write down that they have chosen their position well.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason why I wrote that was the position gave a good field of view of a certain killing area. That's a military area for the best area which you can open fire. The tram had been tracked and it was engaged exactly in the centre of the killing area. Therefore, I assessed it to be a very good position to engage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In serial 25, your report reads that "the firer easily identified the victim, however, because the firer was inexperienced and used an iron sight assault rifle," what is the basis of both the observation that he was inexperienced and that he used an iron sight assault rifle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Distance of 200 metres, with any weapon system in the hands of an experienced sniper would result in an instant kill. The distance of 200 metres is easily accessible. I assessed he used an iron sight for the way the victim was actually hit with the rounds of ammunition and that the firer had not an optical sight but an iron sight, which is much more difficult to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What exactly then in the way the victim was hit caused you to draw this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that the victim actually survived. I would expect the victim would be killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean the place on the body where the victim was hit? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if someone would be very inexperienced but having the I would say the optimal equipment, would it be possible that a person would be hit in that same body part?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If an inexperienced --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If for example, I would have done it?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you were not trained on the equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not trained.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then you would not -- you would probably have the same results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even with another rifle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Serial 26, you write down, "The sniper released a bullet and hit the target having negotiated a small flight path between two buildings and ricocheted from an internal wall into the victim, the sniper was well trained." How do you have to understand this, that well trained snipers can hit someone by a ricochet bullet or -- and would a well-trained sniper be dependent on hitting his target by a ricochet or would you expect him to hit the target directly?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would expect a sniper to hit a target directly. The reason why I said a well-trained sniper was the flight path of the bullet had to go through a very small gap in between two apartment blocks. And that was the meaning from the well-trained sniper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but at the same time you say that the well-trained sniper would not -- would hit the target directly and not by a ricochet?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So one part of the flight of the bullet would make him a well-trained sniper but the actual impact on the location would make him not a trained sniper? Because you say a trained sniper would hit the target directly?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assisted at the target end where the victim was that the sniper actually fired into a light source and not the person, so it was somewhat of an opportune engagement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand your answers. I, at this moment, have no further questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, since at this very stage of the examination of the expert witness, the other judges and I'm stressing at this stage, they have no further questions, you may proceed as I indicated before in the absence of the witness, and I would say that that should certainly not take longer for this first part as to 9.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just to clarify that, Mr. President, when you say in the absence of the witness, do you mean that at this stage I'm not to ask any questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, as I indicated in the absence of the witness the way we would proceed this morning. Before the witness entered the courtroom, I said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- The Court would have additional questions and then you would have an opportunity on selected matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, just to indicate my intention at this stage, I will ask a few questions in relation to some of the issues that you raised yesterday and today, just a few, and then perhaps select randomly one or two incidents to show the way I intend to approach it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir you've been asked some questions yesterday afternoon and then again this morning about incidents number 26. Do you understand from the evidence, as it's been explained to you, that the -- first of all, I think you told us you went to the apartment?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And did you observe that the wall at the apartment through which the bullet entered, at this stage, is glass?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you now understand that the glass wall, whether it was the door section or the window section, was covered to a certain height by wood panelling and above that by some blankets?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You say in your report, the sniper was well-trained and possibly armed with an image intensifier to observe for targets. If the person responsible for firing the shot indeed had an image intensifier, and given the evidence that the television was on, it was a large screen, and it was facing towards that wall, what would you expect the shooter to see through the image intensifier in relation to any breaks in the cover, for instance between the blankets and the walls?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The image intensifier would illuminate the window compared to the rest. Say an apartment next hadn't had the same light source, through the image intensifier the window would be illuminated, shining quite brightly especially at that distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you assist us as to what type of image one sees through the intensifier?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The image given is a black and green image. And light is shown in a light green, kind of white image, and it's almost like a torch.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were also asked questions as to the possibility that the intended target was, for example, next door. Do you understand the evidence to be that the victim and witnesses did not hear any shots preceding the wounding of the victim, nor shots after it?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that assist you at all in determining whether this shot was intentional?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It clearly stays in my mind that the bullet was fired and hit where it was supposed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll take you now to a different incident, about which you have been asked some questions, that is incident 23. The woman aged 44 years, was shot and wounded in her right hand while walking with her father-in-law and they are the words which appear in the schedule to the indictment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Essentially, you were asked how you could eliminate the possibility that the intention of the shooter was only to wound her and not kill her. In your answer, you stated your understanding that snipers are trained to kill and not to wound, essentially I think you said that. Do you understand the evidence also to be that following the wounding, the victim and her father-in-law heard a volley of shots and ran across the adjacent field in order to seek cover?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The fact that the shooting continued and they were forced to take cover, according to the evidence, does that assist you in determining whether the intention was to wound or to kill?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, it clearly states to my mind that they were after killing the individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I will now take you to one of the incidents that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise but the version eight is giving me some trouble, Mr. President, could we please have assistance of a technician, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we get some assistance for Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps number 2, Mr. President, will do. I take you to your report in relation to number 2 and were you asked some questions about this this morning as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be given a copy of -- rather might the witness be given an exhibit tendered through General Karavelic being the sniping maps? I'll just check the exhibit number. It's P3728. In particular, the map for incident 2. Yes, please. I'll be grateful if that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you go to the place as marked with yellow paint, where you were told the victim was shot?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And can you describe briefly, just in a sentence or two, the appearance of that site?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The site had appeared to be a well constructed and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I mean where the victim was shot?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Where the victim was shot was a housing area, an urban area, and quite a close housing area as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can they make breaks between questions and answers? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, as you remember it, the extent of visibility of Serb-held territory from the position where the victim was shot?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President. I object because this question of visibility has no meaning if it is not placed in a context. If we are talking about a foggy day, one cannot see anything, and I believe this way it was phrased, it's a leading question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the witness is testifying on what he saw. Of course, that should be compared with the evidence on whether what he saw on a prior bright day, I take it at least it was a bright day, otherwise you couldn't have seen 895 metres far, of course that can be compared, but the testimony now is about what he saw. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: On both occasions, I actually went to the site, from outside the house you can see clearly the area that was held by the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And did it occupy half of your view or a small portion of your view? Can you give us some idea about that?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The field of view that -- from the house was very good. It was quite a large area, you could see quite a large area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the -- what was the nature of that territory? Was it a plain or a mountain or a ridge or what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the house you could see a very well exposed ridge line which is somewhat wooded and also rocky.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you go to that ridge on either of your visits to Sarajevo for this report?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, did you take a reading with your laser equipment from the area approximately where the victim was shot, as you understood it, to the --

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question, there are two issues, I'd like to you please make breaks because I cannot follow otherwise technically speaking. This is a leading question because we clearly are asking the witness to confirm the presence of an object.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, leading questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Leading questions in this context are surely permissible. The witness has given evidence yesterday that he took readings, the readings are in his report. It is extraordinary that one could object to a leading question in those circumstances. Mr. President, I hope this is not a foretaste of the rest of the day. When the Prosecution has one case, one day, left to finish its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you measure the distance from the approximate area where the -- I'll withdraw that. Was this a case where you could measure the distance from exactly where the victim was shot or had there been some building work which made that impossible?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The area where the victim was shot, there had been no further building work to -- in the line of sight of where the Serbian forces were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Therefore, were you able to measure the distance from where she was shot, as you understood it, to the Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And having regard to your report, was that 895 metres?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you travel to that portion of territory?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Tell us what you saw when you got there?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we arrived to the area where were indicated from the victim's house, with a quick determination of the area, I found positions, built-up positions, of a military nature. For example, an observation post, a sniper hide, and three firing positions with sandbags and empty cartridges.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Let me take you back through that last answer. You Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. told us that you observed --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I really apologise, but last night we did not have time to make observations on the transcript. I have asked courteously to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise. First of all to the interpreters but also for those who have to follow the words in English. These proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you saw that you describe as an observation post?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: An observation post is a -- is a built -- is a manmade feature. You basically dig a hole, waterproof it, hide it, and then live inside it. It is a -- you are given a field of view to cover from this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the waterproofing?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The waterproofing was a thick plastic sheeting which was laid on top of logs, cut logs, and on top of that was turf and soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the significance of the waterproofing?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The waterproofing would enable the persons inside the hide or observation post to sustain themselves for a long period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You told us that you also saw a sniper hide. What exactly did you see?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A sniper hide is the same as observation post. However, it has an opening to the front which enables not only the person inside to see but also to fire from, and that is the only difference. And that is what I saw in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said a few minutes ago that you also saw three firing positions with sandbags and empty cartridges. What do you mean by three firing positions?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The firing positions which I saw were dug holes, manmade dug holes built upwards with sandbags, sandbags to stop any return fire, and prepositioned so they mutually supported each other and covered the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From any of those firing positions, were you able to see the place where the victim was shot?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see the place where the victim was shot in all the firing positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice the calibre of the empty cartridges?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The empty cartridges were somewhat rusted and old, however I assessed them to be of a 7.62 millimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In your report, you say the sniper used a Dragonov sniper rifle. How good was the Dragonov?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Dragonov was, and still is, an excellent sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What size, that is, what calibre ammunition did it use?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It uses variants of the 7.62 millimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You go on to say, and I'll start again at the beginning of the sentence, "It is assessed the sniper used a Dragonov sniper rifle from a well-sighted, company defended location." Why do you say "well-sighted company defended location?"

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the well-sighted was the firing positions, the height, were all placed in locations where they covered the ground in front exceptionally well. I would have placed them in the same place myself. So I presumed that they were well-sighted. A "company defended location" when you dig in and actually surround yourself with area defences that means that you are in a defensive static posture, and a company location was due to the amount of firing positions which were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why could it not have been a platoon, for instance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A platoon position would usually be two or three locations. However, from the area, there were more than three locations which we were not be able to go into for mine reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whether you say mine reasons, was there tape indicating uncleared mine fields?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Further on in your comments on that incident, you say, "It is assessed the sniper was acting on orders from his commander and engaged the non-combatant." Why do you say that you believe or think that the sniper was acting on orders from his commander?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the sniper to be placed in such a position, the commander, whoever he or she may be, would have to deploy the forces there under orders and give reasons why and what to do in eventualities of all actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, I think that will do to give an idea of the approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps one other thing just to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you look at the map on the ELMO? What is the significance of the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red circle was the area in which I found the fire positions and sniper hides.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And perhaps also we see number 11, that is the relevant site indicated on this map for number 11. Does the red circle have any relevance to your conclusions and observations in respect of incident number 11 as well?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assess that incident number 11 was also engaged from the same position, upon getting into the sniper hide at the defended location, you could clearly see both incident 11 and incident 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Therefore, does it follow that the evidence you've given about the suspected source of fire in respect of incident 2 applies to incident 11 as well?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will take a short time to deliberate on the present procedural situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would it be at least ten minutes, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it will take approximately ten minutes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Break taken at 9.26 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered how to proceed at this very moment. First, an opportunity will be given to the Defence for five minutes to comment on the present procedural situation. Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what you mean is just to use this as a base regarding the credibility of the expert witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tell us about the report and testimony until now, so what in your view should be done by the Chamber in respect of this witness and his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Gladly. Well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We all make mistakes today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't trying to be impolite. I'm sorry. Thank you for giving me the floor for five minutes. This is just whether we can apply the rule on false testimony and my observation would be the following. I believe that here, this is a dangerous exercise by the Prosecution, which is in a way something that's been miscalculated, since this expert witness just followed step by step the traces of the Prosecution, not only to completely espouse them but to actually adopt the entirety of the position of the deductions of the Prosecution, I was even going to say the feelings of the Prosecution. Specifically, Mr. President, as I am reading this expert report, quote unquote, I find strange words. How can this witness know, for instance, that some incidents, doesn't matter the number of the incident, on one hand, such and such a sniper would have received orders from his commander to engage non-combatants. Was he there? Did he hear that? Did he find out from the commander? Did he see any written documents, et cetera? And on the other hand, that he had done it, with the objective of killing civilian population. The only thing that's missing here is the word "campaign," but we can see that this expert is the kind of expert that I have called the DSS, so deliberate sniper shot because in all of these cases this is deliberate sniper shot and he goes so far that even when he says there are cases when a machine-gun, light machine-gun or medium machine-gun is used, which is not recognised as being a sniper rifle, it still saying that this is a sniper rifle. So as to the conclusion, I dare not even quote him here. They are as clear as a pike staff, so I find some other very troubling facts. I see that for the last incident, 27, we find surprising terms, not only it is here an issue -- a question of the DSS although it's a machine-gun, but furthermore, we are told, and this is a kind of shelling syndrome which comes in the guise of sniping, is that this was done in a discriminate manner which I suppose was supposed to terrorise the population. Mr. President, this is just a copy of the Prosecution case and the Defence would like to demonstrate this by a series of very specific exact questions to this witness, particularly in terms of his alleged knowledge of weapons and of the alleged intentions of the sharpshooters, and this person goes so far occasionally that there were two of them, that there was some kind of joint shooting, and he obviously couldn't know anything about it, because he was never there at the time when these things happened. So my God, how could we find out whether there was one person or two people? Anyway, all of this is rather fantastic and I believe that the Defence has said enough on what we think of the quality of this witness that we should call an expert witness, but also about his morality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having observed carefully what happened during the testimony of Mr. Hinchliffe, having heard the observations of the Prosecution and having heard the observations of the Defence, the Chamber has decided not to admit the report in evidence. We reject this report not because the Chamber is of the opinion that this witness should have no specific experience but mainly because this report, as it is, does not assist the Chamber in making its determinations. Sources are very often unclear, methodology on many, many conclusions is totally unclear. And apart from that, the report enters very often in a domain which is exclusively the domain of this Chamber, that is to draw conclusions from the evidence presented until now. On the other hand, the Chamber is aware that there might be some factual information that the Prosecution, losing this report, would like to make the subject of questions. The Chamber allows the Prosecution to examine Mr. Hinchliffe, not as an expert witness but as a witness, and as we experienced now and then, even if someone is a normal witness, his expertise could assist him in focusing on certain issues, if I just give an example, I can imagine that from the positions Mr. Hinchliffe might have visited, that he observed that from the presumed firing position, but let's just say from the position he visited, whether it was the firing position or not, that he observed that there was a straight line between one place of an incident, number 2, and another place of an incident, 11. So that would be a factual observation rather than expertise, although I can imagine that especially an expert would see more than a normal person does. So Mr. Ierace, you'll have an opportunity, and we also have to deal with other issues, so I think you have to be very careful how to use your precious time, to see whether you can present factual information from this witness, but the rejection of the report makes it quite clear, I think, that you really should take care that you stay far away from the type of conclusions and the conclusions as we find them in the report. That is how we will proceed. I suggest that we continue, if this is technically possible, keeping in mind that we had a short break of ten minutes, until quarter past 10 to start with, and then have a break. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, a couple of matters. Firstly, I seek your guidance in relation to the application of that finding, to give an example, I had intended to show the witness a segment of the opening video which appears under the title sheet, I think it's "sniping positions" or "sniping from Mount Trebevic," specifically to ask him to identify two types of weapons which appear in that segment. I would be grateful, for instance, if that is now permissible. And no doubt there will be other issues that will arise of a similar nature during my examination-in-chief of him. Secondly, could you give me some indication as to when you will let me know the essence of the reasons for the rejection of the 92 bis statement for Zoran Lesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can imagine that you have specific reasons now to know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the main reason for the rejection of Mr. Lesic's testimony is that the Chamber thinks that the probative value is such that we do not need to receive that information. That has different backgrounds, for example, some portions of the video that was shown in the opening statement, have been admitted into evidence at a later stage. One of the maps, for example, -- one of the photographs was used by another witness and was admitted into evidence. But of course there are remaining photographs, but the Chamber thinks that these do not add to the evidence in such a way that we should hear this evidence or to have this evidence presented at this moment. So the -- I would say the adding to the already-existing probative value of other evidence would be so minimal that, for that reason, we will not use -- that we would use our discretion in such a way that we can do without it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In that case, I suppose we should proceed with Mr. Hinchliffe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the example you gave, you wanted some guidance on that, that would be a question that the Chamber would allow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might I also be advised of the time of the next court break so that I can arrange some meetings during it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think I said that we would have the next break in a quarter of an hour, quarter past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom? [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hinchliffe, in your absence, the Court has given a decision. That decision is that the report you've written will not be admitted into evidence but that the parties can examine you as a witness, and I do understand that Mr. Ierace wants to continue your examination as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, do you still have in front of you the maps or just one?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be given the balance of that exhibit? And might map number 1 be placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, during your visits to Sarajevo, did you go to a spot which is indicated with the number 1 on this map?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take a laser distance reading of the building which is within the red circle on the same map?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was that distance?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And Mr. President, might the witness consult his notes or the report for the purposes of giving the distance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is factual information? Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, this is a factual observation, but usually we don't authorise the witness to use his notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me tell you something, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, about Belgian criminal procedure. If a pathologist would appear in a Belgian court, he would have to learn by heart all the measurements of the dead body. That's not a practical way to proceed. The witness may consult his report just to find the -- to find the measurements. And the Chamber would not mind, Mr. Ierace, if you would like to do this for all the maps, to ask one question and then go accelerated through the maps, if it's just a matter of visiting the spot of the red dot, visiting and measuring and whether the witness could indicate if he visited one or both of these spots.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, for that assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the distance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Distance was 362 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you visit the building which appears within the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not visit it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Was there any obstruction to your line of sight between the red dot and the building in the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take some steps to overcome that obstacle in obtaining your measurement?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Move now, please, to map number 3. Did you go to the site indicated by the red dot with a number 3 indicated?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you go to the area indicated by the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to see the area indicated by the red circle from a position alongside a yellow mark at site number 3?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the distance from that position to the area indicated by the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance was 1.111 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell us something of the nature of the territory within the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red circle had within it an obvious front line position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. I ask you simply to indicate whether it was, for instance, a mountaintop, a valley, a ridge or something of that nature?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a ridge line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please now go to -- I'll ask you another question but pause before you answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I would seek some guidance in relation to the ruling, am I permitted to ask questions of the witness as to his general expertise as a sniper? In other words, not relating to the incidents directly before the Court? Perhaps I would ask the question and then you could indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Hinchliffe, firstly are there books in general circulation which indicate the technical details and capabilities of rifles used by various militaries for sniping purposes?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do those -- is Jane's an example of one such publishing company?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that a book which

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise but for those who can -- who are listening to the Serb and namely our expert, I would be grateful if a pause could be made between the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are those books, to your knowledge, held in high regard?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do those books indicate a maximum range for various types of rifles used by various militaries?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In your experience, how reliable are those maximum ranges when the rifles are used by experienced snipers?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object because so long as the question doesn't relate to a particular weapon, this question doesn't have any precise sense, and there is no point in asking a question about a weapon which is very useful but was never used in the zone in question. So it is necessary in my opinion to rephrase this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm happy to do so, Mr. President.

utterances.text: What was that distance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance was 665 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know the -- and please pause before you answer this question -- the distance of danger, if I can put it that way, from a ricocheting bullet and by that I mean a bullet that hits a hard surface?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance the British army uses is 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Please now go to map number 6. Did you go to the position indicated by red dot and with the number 6 on it?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE

utterances.text: What was the distance?

utterances.text: Distance was 1107 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to ask you some questions about the procedure, in your experience, applied by snipers, and when I use that term in the context of this question, I mean the use of high-powered specialist sniping rifles. When a sniper takes up a position and prepares him or herself for their task, are there any exercises they engage in in order to range their weapon or to use a different description, to prepare it for shooting in a certain target area?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The sniper will try to -- will fire a number of bullets to estimate ranges and the effect the surroundings have on those bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does the sniper do, if anything, with the information that he receives as a result of that exercise?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sniper will fire the bullets, he will measure what he sees to be the distance and also the effects of wind and other weather conditions. He will store this within his own notebook as data.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What adjustments, if any, does the sniper then make to his equipment?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sniper would see the fall of shot, by that I mean where the bullet lands, in respect to where he's aiming and then he would adjust his sight to ensure where he aims, he hits.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If the distance between the sniper and the target area is large, what assistance would you expect a sniper to have in order to acquaint himself with the actual site where the bullets landed during that process?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sniper will usually use a number 2 person. The number 2 is called the spotter. His job is to ensure he locates where the bullets land and therefore tells the sniper, the shooter, the corrections needed to his sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What aids, if any, does the number 2 use?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would use binoculars, laser range finders or a spotting scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you now, please, move to number 7?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, please go to map 13. Did you go to dot 13?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take a measurement?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Of what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the red circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What within that red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the distance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance was 440 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you go to that building in the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you go to any buildings in the vicinity of that red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We went -- we travelled along the road and stopped outside the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we did not go into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know it, the nature of the building?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was expressed to me by the investigator that it was called the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was its appearance, that is, how many storeys?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared to have at least two storeys, possibly an attic area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us if there were any windows or other openings on the side or sides of the building, facing the direction of red dot 13?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now please go to map number 14? Did you go to red dot 14?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take any distance measurement?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Earlier in relation to incident number 4, you gave some evidence in respect of a group of buildings from which you took a measurement. Do you see that same group of buildings on this map?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you point to that group of buildings? And perhaps the map could be panned back, the ELMO camera, rather. Thank you. Do you point to some dark dots in a red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's the only red circle on the map?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us the approximate distance between those buildings and red dot 14? And if you need to use the grid references on the map, please do so.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 1100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. But I'm really worried about the time that is passing. I would have wanted to have the time calculated accurately so that later on, otherwise we won't have the possibility to extend, and we will really be placed at risk in some way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, do you think you could finish by 11.30 approximately? Would that be --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I put it another way? If my learned colleagues don't mind me leading on the distances, I will do my best, perhaps there could be a degree of cooperation. I think I can sense what line I should not cross and we can accelerate the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that I have understood what Mr. Ierace has just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He said that if you are objecting against measuring of distances, and objecting about what is known to everyone here is in a report that was rejected but not for that reason, that it would save time. For example, if you would say all the measurements that would be in the report could be extracted and perhaps provided would be acceptable and any objections against the measurements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is one of the issues that we have, technically speaking, and it's an interesting point because when we take just one measure, generally speaking, it's technically erroneous.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see how far we come.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A word of forewarning, might we have access to P3279V it's an under seal CD. In the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. President, just while it's being set up to save time, we have map number 14, I think we have dealt with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please go to map 15? Did you go to red dot 15?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What measurements did you take from that site and in your answer, indicate to us where they were to?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I visited this site I made two measurements, 490 metres, which was approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you point to a building on the bottom right-hand corner of a U-shaped object within which is written the number 217?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the second measurement? You indicate a building immediately to the right of the base of the triangle, that is the red triangle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go to map 16. Did you go to the red dot indicated with the number 16 and 17?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What measurements did you take?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I measured from the red dot 16 and 17 to the red circle in the bottom left corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say the red circle, was there any particular object?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a small surrounding of buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, this is one of the examples we are pace faced with. This witness just said he made two measurements and, in fact, he only provided one measurement, 490 metres and the second one wasn't given but if we want to do that I think he should provide us with the second figure too, since he mentioned the two measurements in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm grateful to my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the seconds measurement?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 901 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What object did you take the reading from, in respect of map 16 and 17?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A light-coloured building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please look at your screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might that be switched to computer evidence? This is not under seal, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this scene, as relating to incident 16, 17, that is map 16, 17?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As we rotate the photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please tell us when to stop when you see the relevant object.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And can you direct the cursor?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the cursor can come slightly left a little bit right, right, right, keep going right. Stop. And then downwards. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Is that the site?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a group of small buildings, lightly coloured.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, the building or buildings indicated are at the bottom of the road, that is beneath the fall of the -- above the fall of the road, as one looks at the image. If we could move the cursor slightly it appears in the image to be a bright white dot, beneath the transmission lines and approximately halfway between the tarmac road level and the base of the mountains in the distance. Thank you. Might you please to go to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order for -- to be clear in the transcript, it's necessary that with regard to these questions, which concern these documents, it's necessary to maintain the standing objection. I wanted to state that for the benefit of the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Map number 18. Might the witness's video be moved back to video evidence? Thank you. Did you go to red dot 18?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What distances did you measure and to what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I measured from the red dot 18 to the block of flats indicated by a red circle. The measurement was 477 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think on this map there are two red circles. Is the second red circle what you earlier identified as the church? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once more, Mr. President, this is a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, some of your objections, not saying all, but at least some of them, are frivolous. The Chamber might Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. decide, if necessary, to grant one extra day in September to the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you -- would you please go to map 19? Did you go to red dot 19?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What measurement or measurements did you take and of what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From red dot indicated as 19 I measured -- I noticed on the ground at red dot 18 a cone of fire which would indicate the direction of the likely fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What do you mean by a cone of fire?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A cone of fire is the -- is where a group of bullets land from a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And what actually appeared on the ground that you saw?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground was a perfect line approximately 7 metres long, of bullet impact spaces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. What did you sight in order to take your distance measurement?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this cone of fire, it gave me the line of sight. From that line of sight, I just carried ongoing along the line of sight to the far distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What, in the far distance, did you sight?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the far distance was a hillside with various buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to point to that area that you sighted on the map, approximately?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area is -- covers a wide area, I can indicate it as such. The line of sight would indicate in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. For the benefit of the transcript, the witness lays the pointer on the map. Perhaps the ELMO lens could pan back, please? All right. Please lay the pointer on the map again in the appropriate position. That is the pointer is straight and he lays it on the map from red dot 19 at one extremity to one of the red circles, in particular the red circle immediately along side number 90, printed in blue. Thank you. Please go to map 20. Did you go to red dot 20?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Red dot 20, I went to the base of that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take any measurements?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what of?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the base of that building, I took measurements to the red circle, if I may indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Of the three red circles, is it the one in the middle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the distance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance was 760 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go to map 21. Did you go to red dot 21?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What measurements did you take and of what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Red dot 21, I went to that spot and took a laser reading to the building along the line of sight, if I may indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the object within the red circle that you sighted for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institute of the blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. While we are on this map, did you see reference to number -- I'll withdraw that. Please go to map 22? Sorry, did you give us the measurement?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the measurement?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The measurement was 440 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Did you go to red dot 22?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take any measurements?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
