utterances.text: 22 was difficult, and I did not take any measurements.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you travel to any part of the area which appears in the top left-hand quarter of this map?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One sees a road running approximately north-east -- sorry, northwest, southeast, and crossing the two green lines, and passing through the red circle closest to the centre of the map, do you see that road?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please point to it?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Are you familiar with that road?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you travel along it?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us the nature of the buildings, if any, between that same red circle and the green lines in the vicinities of that road?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the buildings to the left and right of that road are somewhat destroyed, with impact marks from both shelling and bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Can you give us an approximate distance from that same red circle to red dot 22?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 800 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go to map 23. Did you go to red dot 23?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take any distance measurements and if so, of what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took a distance measurement from the red dot 23 to an area, if I may indicate?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You point to an area immediately to the left of the dark green line?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the distance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Distance was 560 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go to map 24. Did you go to red dot 24?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take any measurements and if so, of what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From red dot 24, I took a measurement to a building below, to the north of the cemetery and down the hill, indicated with, inside the red circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The cemetery indicated correctly on that the map by that word?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you please point to the building that you sighted for that purpose? Do you point to the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the distance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Distance of 460 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go to map 25. Did you go to red dot 25?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What measurements did you take and of what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From red dot 25, I measured from the position to the institute of the blind, a distance of 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please go to 26. Did you go to red dot 26?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us about a gap between two buildings. Would you point to that gap?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take any measurements from the relevant apartment?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What part of the apartment did you take those measurements from?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the actual incident scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On what side of the glass wall, that is the balcony side or the interior side?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Approximately how far from the glass wall?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was alongside the glass wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you point to the area that you sighted for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area from the original --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The area that you looked at through your laser range finder.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You point to the red circle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the distance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance from point 26 was 352 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Finally go to map 27. Did you go to red dot 27?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what measurements did you take and of what, from red dot 27?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 27, I did not take any measurements. However, I observed the ridge line, which overshadows in the south on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you estimate the distance from red dot 27 to the red circle which appears in the -- that is, the left red circle, the one on the far left, of the group of four?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, that completes examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Looking at the clock, we have a little bit more than two hours, but we need another break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a little bit less than two hours left. The Chamber has considered how much time should be granted for cross-examination. Keeping in mind that part of the time was used by the Prosecution also for -- concerning the expertise of the witness and was not dedicated to the establishment of facts, the Chamber has also noted that part of the examination-in-chief also has been, as to say, of a rather administrative character rather than exploring certain important facts, taken all together, the Chamber has decided that one hour for cross-examination would be fair. So please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We are going to make our calculations again but thank you, in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you answer my questions by saying yes or no each time that this is possible?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before I start putting my questions to the witness, and I didn't say this in order to -- not to interrupt the Prosecution, we have objections to raise regarding the methodology used concerning the maps and we will talk about this at the end of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Are you a ballistics expert, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you an engineer by formation, by training?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you a chemist by training?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, if carrying out an investigation of a ballistics type or criminal type, it's necessary to have at least the following elements. First of all, at least two points in order to trace a line in space; is that correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Secondly, if possible, the minimum material indicia that would be to see the projectile, to see the body, and to see the wound, isn't that the case, yes or no? I'm talking about the principle.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you affirm that it is possible to draw a ballistics conclusion without having seen the projectile, for example? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A ballistics conclusion would need -- you would need to see the bullet, the projectile, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And it is not necessary to see the body?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, let's imagine -- well, I'll rephrase that. Have you ever seen a furrow, within the technical sense of the term, that's the first thing, and have you ever participated in the opening of a furrow?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I did do not understand the name "furrow".

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'll rephrase that question. Do you know what a furrow is, what technically speaking is called a furrow?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, witness, how do you term, in your technical terms, the penetration of a body, if there is an entrance wound and an exit wound? What term do you apply to this?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We simply say entrance wound and exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. That's the entrance and the exit but there is something between the two points. What do you call the part between the entrance and the exit?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do not -- I have not investigated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. In technical terms, that's called a furrow, have you seen a furrow or a canal and have you ever helped with opening up such a furrow or canal?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, you don't know how such -- how such a canal appears, then, what the appearance of such a canal is?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And as a result, you don't know, for example, whether, if you take a certain victim, the canal could be from the upper side to from the bottom or from the bottom up, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, have you ever seen a photograph, and I'm only talking about photographs, of wounds that allegedly were inflicted on all the persons who were involved in the 26 incidents that we mentioned a while ago, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Of the 27 incidents. Witness, have you ever asked to see these photographs, if they existed?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was the response?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not available, or did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, would you agree with me in considering that as a result, given what you have told me, it is absolutely impossible to exclude, given what you have just indicated, the possibility of a ricochet, since, for example, if a canal goes from the bottom up, this would mean that a bullet could have ricocheted from the asphalt --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object on the basis of relevance given the decision of the Trial Chamber in relation to the report, and therefore, the actual evidence of this witness has given. And secondly on the basis that the witness responded to the very first of this series of questions by agreeing that he was not a ballistics expert. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, this witness has a lot of technical experience, of firearms and sniper arms, he says. He was willing to respond to certain questions put by the Prosecution and I think that it is important that we know that it is possible that a canal can indicate the trajectory of a projectile. If this witness can confirm that in principle, this would be a matter of importance for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... All the answers indicate that the witness has got no knowledge whatsoever about that. So what is the use of continuing to question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll rephrase that, willingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct to say that as a result, you are not in a position to indicate, for one of these 27 cases, if we have canals from the bottom up, or if we have canals which are directed from upper side downwards; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not comment on what happened to any of the bodies at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I'm going to move on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to do it, Mr. President for reasons of credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You compiled your report, this report hasn't been accepted. Nevertheless, I have to put certain questions to you. Before writing this report, did you provide the Prosecution with a preliminary report, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You never addressed any kind of preliminary document to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon writing this report, I sent the report to the Prosecution, and then received comment on it. It was not as a draft. It was as the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you modify certain elements in your report, following some comments that were made by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Hypothetically speaking, would you have been asked to underline the deliberate nature of certain acts, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What were the comments that you were given? Could you tell us? And that made you modify certain elements in your report?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The comments refer to factual inaccuracies by myself upon the definition of sniping, according to the pre-trial brief and also ways in which I was not clear in what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am going to stop you, I understand that you are not clear in what you said but you're saying that the Prosecution asked you to go closer to their definition of sniping, is that it?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wrote in the report the definition from the pre-trial brief incorrectly. This was pointed out. And then I amended it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was the definition that was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my recollection, definition of sniping being, if I may refer to my notes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fire from a small calibre weapon, including mortar fire. That was the incorrect line, which I amended to fire from a small calibre weapon, which is, in fact, what I investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Before you compiled your report, sir, did you speak about the methodology with the Prosecution, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The methodology of how I would look at the investigations?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was left to me in how I would conduct my own investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Did the Prosecution -- I withdraw that. For these cases, were you told by the Prosecution such and such cases or such and such incidents seem to be -- seem to be deliberate firing?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The investigator explained what the witness had already said in statements, and then I made my own opinion of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, for each of these cases that we had looked at, did you have two -- from the investigators, the following information, and if you can answer with an a yes or no we would be grateful. First of all, the weather conditions at the time of the incident in question, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Each time, you were given a weather report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a formal weather report, but an indication of the weather at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me what was the weather like for the Taric incident, for instance, which is number 10? Perhaps without consulting the notes but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw that?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Please do. Could you tell us what was the weather like, for incident number 10, please?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you what the weather was like from looking at the date on the incident serial number. I was given a verbal brief in December in my first visit, and I do not remember after 27 briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But for this incident, you are unable to tell us at the time of the firing what was the weather at that time?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have not stated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, Witness, if I ask you the question now for other incidents, is that the case that you will give me a similar answer, in principle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was given a verbal briefing on the ground of each incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But if I ask you -- I don't want to do it in order not to waste time but if I ask you the question in relation to each of the other incidents you would not be able to tell me what the weather was like for each of them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, same type of questions, now, did the Prosecution give you detailed information and then I will ask you specific questions, on combat activities at the time of the incident we are talking about? For incident 1, which combat, incidents 2, which combat so yes or no, did you seek that information?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object on the basis of relevance, the fact that the Defence has an hour does not mean they have to use an hour and there is clearly no, in my respectful submission, no relevance on the basis of the questions to this witness, given what his ultimate evidence has been.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question is obvious. If, one day, we have fierce fighting in the city and this information was not given to the witness, since this witness said that many things also in the first part of his examination-in-chief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it must be quite clear to you that whatever conclusions have been drawn, that's out. We are talking now about where has he been, what measures has he made, did he see trenches or not, but it's especially in the field of conclusions that the Chamber has rejected the report. So, it's of no use to establish that the facts available to the witness were not such that would allow to draw conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that if we examine a bullet and if you know, it would be possible to ascertain whether it had ricocheted; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be able to comment upon that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What you're saying is that this is outside your competence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not qualified to state. So no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, did you ask to see, in order to compile -- or rather did you ask to see photographs of the state of the sites, the way that they appeared at the time of these different problems?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I requested any visual evidence of the estimated fire positions and the weather types, none was forthcoming, because it was not available.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So, you were not in a position to know what were potential obstacles on certain line of fire, that you would be able to establish; is that right, at the time?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just so that I know about the questions, when do we think the next break will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to figure out that, if we would finish by 13.45, I take it we will have a break approximately between 12.30 and 12.45. If you would be able, if this would be possible, for the it technicians as well, because I know that there are limits. If you would be able to finish by approximately 12.30 that would be highly appreciated. That would be just a couple of minutes less than one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. We continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'd like us to look at the projectiles, the technical aspect. Could you confirm, Witness, if you are able to, that a bullet, and I'm talking about a projectile here, so the mobile part, of a -- from a sniper weapon, cannot be distinguished, technically speaking, from a bullet which has been fired with a different weapon but of identical calibre, of course?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have the qualifications to assess that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You're a professional sharpshooter, right?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, however my qualifications and expertise are in the application, the practical application, not in the ballistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, would you be able to tell us whether, in your opinion, and according to your knowledge of a professional sniper, a bullet would be fragmented from an impact in a body much more easily after it has already ricocheted, yes or no, if you know this?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you specify in more detail, the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, for technical reasons we have to break a bit early. So, in a quarter of an hour and then you can complete after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want the break to be taken now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Which is in 15 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will make my question more specific, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know if, yes or no, a bullet, which had ricocheted and which then hits a body of a person, would then fragment much more easily than another bullet which goes directly to its target?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I make the same objection. My learned colleague persists in asking questions which should be addressed it a ballistics expert which this witness is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether fragmentation is a matter of ballistics, but Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, perhaps may I respond? This man is a professional sniper, professional sharpshooter. In his report, you could see that he was speaking about formidable hits by ricochet and so on. He certainly know knows about ricochets and the reason why what I want to say about this is that if the answer was yes, then we could conclude certain things from there. If bodies were examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not understand. This is rather a matter of forensic pathology or the expertise of a -- of someone who does a post mortem than anything else. Do you know anything about the way bullets impact on bodies and because you told us something about this before, do you have any specific knowledge on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no specific knowledge on the way a ricochet has an effect on a body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in general, any knowledge on the effect of bullets on bodies, such as we talked before, about the canals?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But similar subjects?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to come back to some other elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, here I'm going to have to make a distinction, sometimes not so clear, between fact and conclusion in relation to this, and I would be grateful in advance if you have any guidance for me, that you think might be useful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you stated at least on two occasions, I believe, that you knew that it was an established fact that such and such a sniper had received an order from his commander to attack or to fire at targets that were, in your terminology, the way you put it, non-combatant targets?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if my friend persists in asking these questions and is permitted to do so, then, as has happened in the past, if he opens the door to the report being tendered, I will take that opportunity. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think that it has become quite clear from the questions from the Bench as well, whatever --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... And of course, if you do not know about the orders, then you cannot -- it's -- that is exactly the area where the Chamber has decided that an expert witness cannot enter into the domain which is exclusively for the Chamber. So, the witness has no direct knowledge of that and we will have to determine on the basis of the evidence, and to the extent necessary, whether victims were civilians or not or combatants on the way home or eating soup in their kitchen. So that's exactly the area which the Chamber not accepted to be within the domain of this witness on the basis of his expertise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, on the basis of what, and I believe that this question is outside of this area, on the basis of what could you, as a general rule, exclude or rule out the possibility of a stray bullet and -- what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, there is an English saying that something goes without saying. You have already, for a month, asked people to exclude for 100 per cent certainty whatever a witness would answer to that question. It would be quite clear, independent of what the answer is, that something you cannot exclude such thing for a full 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is clear for the Chamber, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What one can exclude for certain is usually in very specific circumstances is clear for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We are going to show some documents later on to this witness, but I'd like to ask technical questions no, Witness. Did you examine the structure of Dobrinja -- screens, Dobrinja screens?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... [In English] For the translation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you examine the structure of the embankments in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you provide further assistance into how you mean to look at the structures? How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you have a look what this structure was made of? Was this a concrete canal or was this made of soil?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I ask you, does this regard to incident number 6? I'm clearing my head on which area you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm talking about the river, the Dobrinja river. There is an incident which occurred on the Dobrinja river. Did you examine this embankment in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area about incident 6, I did look and examine the impact area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you examine these embankments?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only where it was indicated the victim was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You were not curious to look up a bit, what this canal looked like?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I specified on the incident locations only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So that your answer, that means no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did observe the canal area but only where the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Therefore, no, you did not look higher up, what the embankment or the river bank was made of, right?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, did you go to the famous tower, the clock tower of what we know as the church?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, so you did not go to the top of the tower and look at the view?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, so you were not able to examine, from the top of the bell tower, if there was, yes or no, a probable firing angle on a location that you were shown?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go to the church or the bell tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you were told, you were asked to speak of earlier about an incident in relation to which you went near a window, and you would have seen buildings opposite the window. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, were you given any kind of information, at the time that you went there, on what was happening at the time of the incident, on the site, on the location, of the buildings that we can see in the perspective, in the view from that window?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information I was given was where the front lines were at that point in time, and which side of the -- both forces were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But no information regarding possible combat at the time?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no specific indications.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I'm also referring to the answer that you gave in relation to this scene from a window which was illuminated by a television screen. Do you see that image in your mind?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you stated that it was not possible to hit anything else but that, because this was the window which was lit?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I withdraw the objection. I don't make any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. How could you know that at that time, hypothetically, there were not other viewers watching TV in other rooms, or someone who had something else on which would make something else light up?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I obviously can't state what was happening at the time since I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that your conclusions are mistaken in a sense that you don't know whether there were other sources of light?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we are talking about the facts on which the witness testified. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, if I dare ask you, very frequently I don't hear what you're saying because I think you start before I finish in some way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I should not do that but sometimes I have to intervene but next time, I will ask you first to stop, then make a short break, and then say whatever I have to say. Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Speaking of a break, perhaps this would be an ideal time to have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn for 15 minutes and we will resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you, Mr. President. I don't want to lose too much time. How much time remains for us, more or less?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Not any more than until ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the usher assist us and Madam Registrar so that very soon we can provide a document to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In the interval, the Prosecution showed you 26 or 27 maps, I think. You saw that a minute ago, and I would like you to answer these questions. When you were shown these maps, Witness, were there no indications on it, yes or no? Was it unmarked?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which maps are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm referring to the 26 or 27 maps that we saw a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maps in which I used, yes, they are the ones, yes, the only indications were the incident numbers, the red circles and the lines of confrontation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you said, "Red circles," do you mean that you put the dots there yourself or they were already there?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dots were already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And the linear indications were they already that map?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which indications?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The linear indications, for example, the firing, the possible firing zones, et cetera, et cetera, such as these linear indications here. Were they on the map already?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the legend was that on the map, too?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would we agree that this map was presented to you, and when it was presented to you, had been preprepared, it had already been prepared?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had been prepared, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, did you climb the towers, the high buildings, the towers, such as the buildings that can -- that were mentioned in incident 5?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you were never in a position to observe possible shots, the alleged possible shots, from these positions?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I visited a number of incidents where I went inside an apartment block, in the apartment where the alleged incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. My question was the point of fire, the place from which fire was opened.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, with regard to incident 5, which took place near the Tito barracks, I think, did you receive any indication of fighting in that area, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was give an indication by the investigator about fighting and an indication from the investigator, from what the witness had said, where the forces were on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. My question wasn't the establishment of the forces but the existence of fighting at the time of the incident, of the alleged incident, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was given that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, what fighting was going on?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told of known positions and fighting was in and around the area, it was very generalistic information given.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What position?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In and around the towers and the subsequent area and the use of towers, as indicated by local knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. But now you're talking about sniping. Very well. I am talking about fighting, about other combat, which allegedly took place in the area. But this is something to be distinguished from sniping.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not given that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know if, by some extraordinary circumstances, there is any testimony according to which the fire, the shot, was fired from the second floor, allegedly, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I understand the question to be: Was the building indicated in a statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you ever told, with regard to this tower block, that the shot may have been fired from the second floor, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No floor was identified to me, and the positioning of the firing point, as assessed by myself was after my own investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you ever see anyone in Sarajevo, who might have been able to confirm personally the existence of this technique which concerns the removable brick?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within Sarajevo, when I visited, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, have you been through the streets of Sedrenik, are you familiar with these streets?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you walked down these streets?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection of which area you're referring to, without showing it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you can't know specifically whether from such and such a street in Sedrenik it might be possible to see certain positions from where fire was allegedly opened? You can't confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm, I don't know the area which you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you that the word Sedrenik does not say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not, whilst I visited I was taken to the various incident spots. I do not have a knowledge of each street name and is so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand you. You might have been to Sedrenik without knowing what Sedrenik is?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could we take the document that you have in front of you? Can you show me the document that you have? That's not the document I wanted to give you. Put that document aside. Don't go through the pages. Thank you. Thank you. Witness, you now have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Is this 173 or 17 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 173, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we get a copy for Mr. Ierace as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Not for the first time, the Defence has conspicuously failed to abide by its obligations under Rule 67(C), the Prosecution has not previously received either of these documents by way of reciprocal disclosure and to - I should say - deliberately leave the showing of these documents to the witness to the last five minutes of his cross-examination, and then seek to question him on them, is in my respectful submission, a flagrant breach of their responsibilities and I object to the witness being asked any questions about such documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, did you disclose these documents to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President, could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you disclose these documents to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but we won't produce them. That will be a lot simpler, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you affirmed the existence of Dragonovs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I take the question to be, do I understand Dragonov rifles exist?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That they exist in the Sarajevo universe?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Did you ever see a single Dragonov in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you ask the question as to whether I was there with this organisation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you ever shown by any authority a Dragonov rifle?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in my experience as a whole?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know who manufactures the Dragonov rifles?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Principally from data, then, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the transcript isn't clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who is the manufacturer, who produces this weapon?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapon is produced by various nations, they all come from the family of Kalashnikov rifles, AK range and were to the best of my knowledge originated from the Soviet Union.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: According to what factual elements -- on the basis of what factual elements can you claim that some of the weapons from which fire was opened were Dragonov rifles and I'm referring to your personal experience and not what you have heard or learned from other sources?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, on being deployed to Bosnia in 1993, I attended a pretraining package which focused on mines, equipment, weaponry, known in the area. Intelligence briefings from given to me regarding the Dragonov.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If I said that there were never any Dragonovs in the -- among the former weapons of the so-called JNA army, what would your reaction be?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would -- that would contradict what I had previously been told by my organisations, prior to my deployment in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Might it be possible that certain individuals obtained such weapons?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons, the AK range as a whole, is used by various armies, factions, countries throughout the world, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm not talking about armies. I'm talking about individuals. Could it be possible that individuals might have obtained such arms, me, for example, others, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Piletta-Zanin appears to be putting to the witness that the accused's subordinates did not have Dragonovs. If that is what he's putting to the witness, he has not put it previously to a number of witnesses in the Prosecution case who have given evidence to that effect. On that basis, in my respectful submission, the questions should be disallowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But may I ask you, Mr. Ierace, was it ever put into evidence that Dragonovs were sniper rifles used by subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. For example, one example is through General Karavelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I haven't got that clearly in my mind but I think that there are two different issues at this very moment, Mr. Ierace. I think one is the one you mention but the other is whether private individuals could obtain such weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And Mr. President, that's why I used the word appears with some emphasis because when one looks at the questions as a group, that appears to be what he's putting obliquely to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so perhaps the -- ask that to the witness. Do you know whether private individuals could obtain, buy or whatever way, Dragonov rifles, sniping rifles?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Another two questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if you never saw the rifle or the rifles from which fire was opened, would you agree with me that any consideration, any consideration with regard to the range, is purely speculative, it's just a hypothesis, if you don't know which weapon was used? Would you agree with that? Would you come to the same conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that my findings are based on detailed accounts of weapons used from such publications as Jane's and so on. But I do not know which weapon, for sure, was used in each incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. And that means that if you didn't know which weapons were allegedly used, nothing can be deduced as to the range of the weapon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You can deduce the range of a shot without knowing what weapon was used to fire the shot?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We have an indication from a witness as to where the shot heard -- I was therefore give and range and the range indicates the type of weaponry, in fact in some cases the ammunition used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, and my very last question. It's the last one. Witness, do you know how many joules [Realtime transcript read in error "jules"] You need to penetrate a body?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a ballistics expert. I can't tell you how many joules it takes to penetrate a body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the last question, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, very well, because the transcript says "jules," but we were referring to "joules".

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One question in re-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A minute or so ago you said in response to a question regarding your knowledge of the range of rifles that you relied upon publications such as Jane's. In your experience, how reliable is the maximum effective range of rifles as indicated in Jane's and similar publications?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to experienced firers, then it is unreliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that unreliability upwards or downwards, in other words is the effective range, in your experience, higher or lower than indicated in those publications with experienced riflemen?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Experienced snipers will undoubtedly outshoot what is stated in these publications. If I may give an example, the L96 British sniper rifle is indicated by Jane's as to being 900 metres accurate fire. Whereas myself, and the people who I train, can hit a target actually over 1.000 metres with the same equipment. It's experience of the individual and the firer, which breaks these barriers put before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has one question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Just one question. Which is the average velocity, speed, of a bullet, of a rifle, sniper rifle bullet?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without referring to data, I could not give you an accurate answer off the top of my head. I'd have to refer to manuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I was thinking in a sniper firing from a more than one kilometre away, how can he calculate the target, moving target, for example?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two methods of shooting a moving target. There is the tracking method where you follow the individual or object, placing the cross-hairs in front of the person or object. There is the shocker method, where you give yourself a killing area, an area in which you want to engage the target and allow the person or individual to progress into that area and then you open fire. When you decide which method to use, you have to understand how far away you are and guess where you need to aim. For instance, if you're closer to the target, then the shocker method would be better, i.e., the person -- you can keep your point of aim on the person as such. If you're further away then it's a real guess, as you fire the rifle, you cannot guess the speed and how long it will hit the person in front. You just use your data from experience from training as to what you need to place in the cross-hairs and then you fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has one question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] This is just a clarification, please. You said in relation to an aid for vision or for sight, you called it, you said a sighting scope, that that was one of the methods in order to have a sharper view of things. You said that spotting scopes were used. Could you please explain what did you mean by that, by the spotting scope?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: A spotting scope is used by the second person within the pair. The way most armies throughout the world deploy snipers is as a two-person formation, so you have a firer and a spotter, two people. The firer obviously fires the weapon system, the spotter observes and corrects the firer. The spotter will use either a pair of binos, binoculars, or a spotting scope. In the case of a spotting scope, what the observer sees through the spotting scope is exactly the same what the firer sees so they will have the same sight pattern so the same cross-hairs. And what he will do is he will see where the bullet lands, if possible, on the person or around the area, and then deduct, by using the sight picture, where he needs to aim or how he needs to adjust his sight to bring on line the rifle to the target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, you said these are two people, two snipers, two sharpshooters who are not -- who are next to each other and give each other information on two positions or would it be in one single position next to each other?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would generally be in one position. A rule of thumb, which the British army uses, is to fire one sniper round it takes two people. However, in some instances, a firer can shoot by himself if he's confident in his own ability. And if he feels he can see where his bullets are actually landing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, in the event that there is only one bullet that was fired, so you with rule out that these would be non-professionals and if you say that the norm is that there should be two of them, and there has only been one single bullet, we can then presume that this was someone who did not belong to a hierarchy, a specific hierarchy, or would you rule out this possibility?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFFE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct, no. One round would be fired. However, -- so one person would fire but two people would evaluate the factors in firing the rifle. If, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hinchliffe, it will not surprise you that I have put already so many questions to you that I have no further questions for you. That means that this concludes your evidence in this Court. I'd like to thank you very much for having come and having answered during yesterday and today the questions of both parties and of the bench. Thank you for that. And I hope you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, could you please escort Mr. Hinchliffe out of the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The next matter, Mr. President, is the tender of the 17 items from the bar table, by letter dated the 23rd of July, 2002, I informed the Defence and the Trial Chamber of each of those items. I think they are 16 documents and one videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Normally, the way we tender material is to provide multiple copies of each item. I imagine that if we did that in relation to these items it would consume much of the remaining time. I wonder if I could respectfully suggest an alternative, that since the Defence has been provided in advance by the Prosecution with copies of each of these documents and the video, and a transcript of the video, that perhaps they could indicate if they have any objection to any of the items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's, as a matter of fact, what I was intending to ask them. So we have in front of us at this very moment the list attached to the letter of the 26th of July, 2002, concerning tendering, from the bar table, the documents mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Minor correction, Mr. President, 23rd of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do agree, but on the 26th of July, you did send another list of the same documents. May I ask -- perhaps first, Ms. Pilipovic, I think your expert's presence in this courtroom is not necessary anymore. May I indicate, this is a public hearing so whenever you want to follow what happens in this courtroom from the public gallery, you're quite welcome to do so but, yes, unless you'd like him to be present when we are dealing with the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether we are going to need, we will probably need that in relation to documents so perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If you need him for that perhaps that should have been a better order to do but since we started with the other issue and since it's all public I think that the expert could just stay in the courtroom. May I hear from the Defence -- okay. I've taken a wrong order, as a matter of fact. I think it would be better to first deal with the documents tendered during the testimony of Mr. Hinchliffe. Madam Registrar, there are no, as far as I'm aware of; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there was only the report, I took the wrong order but it doesn't change anything because there are no documents tendered, since the Defence withdrew the two documents that were already on our table. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I understood well that the maps, as such, will not be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Evidence. As you might have noticed, the maps shown to the witness were those who were corrected, I think, by General Karavelic but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's so, Mr. President and at that stage, you indicated that the markings on the map which would be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would be ignored.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I should say formally that I seek to tender the red dots and the red circles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's something on which the Defence could express its opinion. Because until now we accepted the maps but we ignored the red part of it through this witness we would then, since his testimony is about the red dots and the red circles we would pay attention to that as well. So if there is any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That was the reason why I allowed myself to stand up. There is a categorical objection here to, shall we say, the transfer of these maps into the area of testimony of Mr. Hinchliffe, for the following reason. This witness himself, personally, he did not know anything about confrontation lines, about combat areas, about firing positions, possible firing positions, or about the injured and the casualties. So, that is really in opposition to all the other people, like, for instance, the general who recorrected the map, because he himself had a personal knowledge of certain facts, professional knowledge, like combat lines, confrontation lines and so on. Now, we believe that in this case of Witness Hinchliffe to have slipped him a map where he had nothing else to do except to say, "yes there is a red dot, yes this is the incident, the circle and so on," that is not the right way to proceed. That is precisely the written version in colour, which is forbidden in oral testimony. So that's the reason why this is a leading -- and it's not acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... While tendering, I would say, the red part of the maps, do you seek to tender that in order to show to the Chamber the places indicated to the witness, Hinchliffe, when he visited the area and also assisting the Chamber to know exactly what places were visited by Mr. Hinchliffe? Is that it or by giving us maps with red dots would that be in your view evidence that could establish where the witness was, became a victim, or where the fires were shot from? Sometimes we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly not, Mr. President. The extent of the evidence of this witness is as you have expressed, and of course, that then becomes -- that then ties in with evidence of other witnesses in order to arrive at those ultimate conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear. We will give a decision on that. We have no other exhibits in respect of Witness Hinchliffe. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin??

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as the formulation was a little too precious, at least as far as I'm concerned, it is clear that for the Prosecution, as far as the Prosecution is concerned, they don't want to prove anything in relation to the existence of victims and the -- where the firing was coming from and all that. This is how I should understand it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that what is expressed on that map is what the Prosecutor thinks that would be a correct reflection of the evidence available and since you can't ask a witness or an expert witness to say, "Well, just look around Sarajevo and see whether you can find any spot where someone might have been injured or killed," that they used this map in order to bring Mr. Hinchliffe, who doesn't know anything from his own knowledge of what happened at that time, to bring to that places and see what he, as an experienced sniper, would observe. I think that's the position. Of course, if that contradicts other evidence, the Chamber then perhaps, if it would be admitted in evidence, would say, "well, this is not correct because it really contradicts what is in evidence given by other witnesses." And if it combines, then of course, the Chamber might think that the dots on the basis of the evidence available were at least not put in the wrong places. Let me put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will give a decision on that. Then we return to the issue we used before. But perhaps, Mr. Ierace, since that might assist you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, at this moment, I think that since we've dealt with the document, that is, your expert is -- I take it is excused by you and could leave the courtroom and is of course welcome to follow what happens in this Court. Perhaps, Mr. Ierace, I read a part of the decision presumably be filed in respect of -- the Chamber in respect of Mr. Lesic. Considering however that the date when various photographs were tendered -- various photographs tendered were taken.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If any, no objection was raised by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm making the same mistakes, and I sincerely apologise, as everyone else has done before. I restart. However, that the date when various photographs tendered were taken is of very limited value, if any, as no objection was raised on this basis by the Defence, that the document marked MFI3 is already in evidence, that the photograph marked MFI2 does not go to the proof of any specific facts and constitutes at most an useful tool to understand the geography of Sarajevo, an aspect for which much evidence was already adduced, that the collage video presented during the opening statement does not tend to prove any specific incident, but rather tries to convey the general atmosphere that prevailed in Sarajevo during part of the period covered in the indictment, I add to that that of course parts of the video were admitted into evidence and were then more specifically discussed, this would be I think the most important part of the decision on Mr. Lesic that you can expect to be filed later today. Let me then turn to the exhibits to be tendered from the bar table and ask the Defence whether there are any objections and what the objections would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. This may surprise you, but at the time the Defence does not know this yet, and why we don't know it is because we would have wanted, on an important issue, we would like to hear what the Prosecution has to say on the way this cassette was made. I don't know whether you're able to examine it. We were able to do it together, Ms. Pilipovic and myself, but this is a montage of several elements, apparently, we don't have the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you referring to number --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2347. That is the only cassette, and Mr. President, the problem is the compilation of sources. We don't know where these pieces of information, video information, come from. We don't know whether this is just an excerpt from a longer passage or this has been put together, and what's been made is some kind of patchwork, and we were very frequently not able to see the dates of the interventions. So, perhaps Sherlock Holmes would be able to make something out of it but I'm afraid I don't really have his stature. So first of all I want to know from the Prosecution, this piece from this source, this origin and so on and so on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace. First of all, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, did you ask such information, not to Sherlock Holmes but to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the problem is that we really had not much time this week, and we did it as a -- on a nightly seance, if you'll allow me to say, that but we see things as we are discovering them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you respond to this not yet objection but.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will. No. First of all the tape was disclosed to the Defence on the 26th of November, 2001. I don't know whether Your Honours have seen the tape. I imagine not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we have not received it. We have not seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The tape consists entirely of interviews of General Galic, with the exception of the first segment which is a press conference where the speaker is primarily General Abdel-Razek and General Galic is seated alongside him. Mr. President, an even more obvious source of information than the Prosecution as to what the -- what date the interviews relate to was the accused himself. As to the source of the material, it's public-source material. It comes from a variety of sources, one would think, in the form of televised interviews, interviews with General Galic, carried, it would seem, on local Serbian TV. As to specific information as to where each segment came from, I cannot assist but the first issue is, surely, is it relevant and, if it is, does the accused deny that it is, indeed, himself speaking the words and appearing in the video? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, to your knowledge, has there -- been any cutting or pasting or if you're talking about an interview, would that be parts of an interview or the interview as being broadcasted?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I viewed the video with the benefit of the transcript, and it seems to be a series of videos -- I'm sorry a series of interviews, short interviews, or statements made by General Galic without any apparent editing other than the editing one would expect on the segment that went to air. Certainly no abrupt cuts on that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you tell us if it has been televised? Someone should have recorded it and having brought it to the attention of the Prosecutor's Office, do you know who did so or --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't, Mr. President. I don't know how it came into -- how the various segments came into our possession. I could certainly make some inquiries over the break and inform the Defence of the results of those inquiries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there is not a lot of break. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I simply make the point that it's simply General Galic being interviewed and making statements. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this brings ME to complete my initial intervention. This is about General Galic, yes, but we don't know when, we don't know in which conditions this was filmed, this was produced. And even the Prosecution says they don't know what this is about. Now, in these circumstances, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask you, it's not -- you say it is General Galic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that that's what the Prosecution says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Dispute. Do you say it's another person, a lookalike or something like that, sitting next to General Abdel-Razek or perhaps General Abdel-Razek is also a lookalike?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence, as we stand and speak here, we believe that General Abdel-Razek was there. This cassette should have been produced before General Abdel-Razek so that we were in a position to ask questions. Now, to tender at the very last minute, a document which would involve General Galic without -- General Abdel-Razek without giving him the possibility of saying anything whatsoever is equally serious as what I tried to tender earlier which provoked a very strong reaction. On the basis of this, we are not able to accept this, to criticise, contest, and to look for the truth, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should say something in response to one of my learned colleague's submissions. He said the cassette should have been produced before General Abdel-Razek so that he would in a position to ask questions. It was placed on the exhibit list. It was disclosed to the Defence. Time did not permit the Prosecution to play it, but the Defence had every opportunity to cross-examine General Abdel-Razek about that interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having heard the argument of the parties on the video, let us turn to the other documents. Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
