utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We have similar difficulties here. We received a rather thick load of documents, and we did not have time to examine them in detail, we just had a -- we just glanced at them but this way of producing documents without leaving the possibility, particularly in the last ten minutes of the trial of the case, to allow the Defence to question and cross-examine this way is not acceptable. There are, in here, elements which could be useful for the Prosecution's case. Otherwise, they wouldn't be here. But, however, we don't have the possibility, certainly not in the few minutes that we have left, to go to the bottom of the case, and to furnish, if this was necessary, our own counterarguments, counterdocuments, I think a lot of time has been lost, without the fault of the Defence, but the Defence cannot then be accused of wasting time. The way the Prosecution has done, in a direct way, that Defence has just been handed, slipped under the door, very thick load of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have to consider the matter. And give you a decision on the shortest notice. We might even deliberate on the issue right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we would deliver it right away, may I just ask the parties whether there is anything else that -- the Chamber is aware that they still have to take a decision on the admission of Exhibit P3738O. Which is document, one out of a batch on a person named Maksikovic [phoen]. Is there any other issue that urgently needs the attention of the Chamber at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I take it that you're contemplating withdrawing to make a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might I just say a few quick things that might be appropriate at this stage? Firstly, in relation to the video, it's apparent from the content of the interviews that they all relate -- they were all recorded during General Galic's tenure as the corps commander, and therefore, they were all recorded in the indictment period. Secondly, in response to my friend's argument that these documents should have been tendered through a witness, the reason they are being tendered by the bar table is because none of them lend themselves to a particular witness. They are public documents, nothing more than that. In relation to other outstanding issues that you might wish to consider in your absence, the Prosecution received, five weeks ago, a large bundle of documents from the Defence by way of further reciprocal disclosure. That bundle will take sometime to interpret, to translate, rather, so that we can determine if we wish to tender any. Yesterday, the Defence handed us an additional 94 documents by way of reciprocal disclosure, the day before the Prosecution case ends, all untranslated. That will require some further attention. There is a third bundle, Mr. President, that you may recall, from earlier this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. My basic point is this. There is a number of documents which, through no fault of the Prosecution, require more time to consider, to analyse, and indeed, fundamentally to translate. I, therefore, say this: That it may, and I emphasise may, not will, it may be the case, assuming the Prosecution case finishes today in 15 minutes, that when we reconvene, the Prosecution will seek leave to reopen its case, leaving aside the question of Zoran Lesic, solely for the purpose of tendering documents from one of those three bundles, and I emphasise may, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just in response to the last comment made by Mr. Ierace, could the Prosecution inform us who the journalists are who conducted these interviews? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the transcript sometimes identifies the relevant agency. To give an example, in the transcript, in relation to one of the segments, the interviewer starts off by identifying himself as coming from, I think it's Republika Srpska television, and he also indicates the title of General Galic in the interview, but essentially, I can't go beyond what's in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can't give the name of the journalist, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will deliberate on the issues pending at this moment but perhaps before doing so, I'd like to inform the parties also about what, if we conclude the presentation of the Prosecution's case by today, as indicated before, the Defence will have seven times after the -- seven days after the recess to file its -- to file its no case to answer motion, if they want to do so, so that would be seven full working days available, seven full days, it should be filed by the 2nd of September. The Prosecution will then have two weeks to respond. The Chamber seriously considers to have a hearing held on or around the 20th of September, and independent of what our decision will be, we don't know the motion, we don't know the content of the motion, we do not even know to sure whether it will be filed or not, although the Defence has, several times, indicated that it would file such a motion, the Defence should prepare, in case a motion will be filed, and not be totally granted to start the presentation of its case on the 7th of October. One additional aspects of a motion to dismiss, 35 pages would be inclusive all attachments. So the Chamber does not expect a document of 35 pages with 100 other pages attached to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, a number of matters very quickly. I think you required the Defence to file a list of witnesses and exhibits today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Today, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Secondly, outstanding decision, Mr. Kavcic [phoen], that Rule 92 bis issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the decision will be -- as you know the decision was postponed since whether or not Witness AK would testify might have been of some importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The decision I hope can be filed today as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Also Witness AK's documents, I think there is an outstanding decision there. I think that's it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me. AD, not AK. No. AK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have a -- we had a new translation on lists, medical lists, because there were differences in translation. That was P3748.1. We asked for a translation, and I think that -- did we take a formal decision on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, what had happened is we had gotten a draft translation and we are trying to get a certified translation, not a draft. We got a translation and we are in the process of checking it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We asked whether the draft will be the final translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is a draft okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says "draft translation".

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have regard to issues of time. I'm wondering if, although P3748.1 is a draft translation, if it could be received in evidence. I don't know if the Defence has any objection to any aspect of the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It really is a list of names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a specific objection against the draft translation as it has been tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must admit that I can't remember that right now. Could I see it physically, if this is possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Use the time when we are deliberating it to see whether there is any specific objection on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is another matter. Given the time, now ten minutes, I do formally seek leave to reopen the Prosecution case, or - I'm sorry - I do formally seek leave to continue the Prosecution case into part of the first day back, in order to call Zoran Lesic to give short evidence in relation to a few of the photographs and videos referred to in his 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that would be, I take it, specifically on when the videos were taken, the spot, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I never had heard any specific dispute. A lot of objections against whether 360 degrees photo was --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It won't be repetitive at all about that. It's the matters that have not been introduced into evidence at all, such as the scene in the opening video which the Prosecution says where the woman is shot, the Prosecution says that's the same intersection which is involved in incident 5 and therefore, is further evidence of that intersection being a source of civilian sniping. It's that type of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask what the response of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say yes, that means no, Mr. President. I can't imagine that in ten minutes, towards the end of the case, that we can ask for this to be reopened for something that we've had a lot of time to do. The best things have to come to an end. And Defence -- the Defence can't accept reports which are very costly for the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. international community and for the Defence as well. Our position is no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a matter of reopening. The Prosecution asked extension of time and say that the presentation of its case will not be concluded. That's a different thing from reopening because before you can reopen something, you have to close it first. The Chamber will be back. Would the interpreters at this very 2nd of August still be there if you would need ten to 30 minutes and then give our decisions? I'm aware that I have great admiration not only with respect to the speed the speakers developed and how you dealt with it and this is not bribing you? But it's a real sincere expression of the appreciation of the Chamber. Would you still be there if we return in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To hear your answer, I have to change to either channel 4 or 5.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. --- Break taken at 1.37 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber owes the parties a few decisions. Let me first give you the decision on, if I could call that, the red part of the maps, the maps on the incidents. These are 28 maps that were already admitted into evidence, Madam Registrar, under number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The red circles and red spots are no longer excluded, as it was decided before, the Chamber will pay attention to that, but only to the limited sense as the Chamber understands the tendering of this aspect of the map. That means only in direct relation with the testimony of the witness Hinchliffe. Then we owe you a decision on the list of documents and one video, tendered from the bar table. The documents are admitted into evidence. These are items number 5, 8, 10, 13, 58, same as 56, 82, 153, 276, 1472, 1591, 2073, 2293, 2324, 2465, 2858, 3150. These are the documents. If the Defence, not being fully aware that these would be tendered from the bar table, would have any objections as to the content, or the authenticity, of these documents, an opportunity will be given, at least you have the opportunity to make that objection in a latter stage but not later than the 26th of August, and in writing. Then we have the video, that is 2347, same as 340. We have heard some objections by the Defence, in order to -- the objections were, to some extent, vague, to some extent, they were less vague, where it was said that the Defence was not convinced that it would not be a montage. We heard the response from the Prosecution, and the Chamber thinks it necessary to look at the video itself in order to decide on the admissibility in evidence of that video. Therefore, the video is tendered. A decision will follow. Then, there was still pending a decision on document P3738O which is a medical document. It is not admitted into evidence as it is now. There is almost a full translation of, in the original language, illegible parts of the document that might be a form, and someone might think that that would have been the text, which is illegible, but that is not what a translation is supposed to be. Therefore, it is not admitted into evidence, but if the Prosecution would be able to present a legible copy, the Chamber will then consider to accept that in evidence, and that should not be later than the 26th of August. Then we still -- there was a still another request from the Prosecution to have a document that was admitted into evidence through Witness D be returned to that witness and be replaced by a photocopy. That request, having been no objections against that, at least the Chamber is not aware of any objections. It was a written submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on condition that the photocopies are good, not as they have sometimes been, the Defence has no objections to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will personally look after the quality of the photocopies so there is no need to be worried about that. Then the request is granted. Then finally, I'd like to inform the -- yes. The request to call Mr. Lesic or to have extra time granted is denied. That would also mean that, at this moment, apart from a few pending decisions on issues that have been raised, that we take it that the Prosecution now has concluded its case, everything being dealt with. Yes, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and just one other matter. In relation to some submissions on the law in respect of a certain matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll tell you something about that perhaps you might need to turn to closed session for one second for that. Then that relates to, I would say, the future development of the case. I'd like to indicate to the Defence when preparing their case, it's absolutely certain that not more time will be granted to the Defence to examine their witnesses as has been granted to the Prosecution. That means until this very moment approximately 170 hours for examination-in-chief. That's the time that was used by the Prosecution. So, that is a guidance for the Defence. Then we turn into closed session for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. I do understand that there are no other outstanding issues, yes, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, formally, it gives me great pleasure to say that, subject to those outstanding decisions, that completes the Prosecution case. And secondly, might I remind you of the requirement placed on the Defence to provide a list of witnesses and exhibits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's been discussed, I think, several times also with the representative of the Senior Legal Officer and I understood that we will receive such a professional list at this very moment; is that correct, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is quite correct, you have seen that one of our assistants is present and is taking care of this matter and it is a pleasure for the Defence to provide the Prosecution with a new binder and we know that they will make the usual good use of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, being at the end of the Prosecution case, and just at the beginning of the recess, I first of all would like to thank, once again, because the Chamber is well aware that we did high -- put high pressure on both those who assist us outside the Court, but perhaps also a considerable pressure on those who have to work in this Court. And therefore, I wish you a very good holiday and I hope that you will be able to relax and to take your time so that we can start fresh at -- after the recess. I'm also aware, General Galic, that wishing a nice holiday is not what could be -- I could wish you. The Chamber is fully aware that being in detention is a situation with -- which is hard, and especially now when we leave for holidays, the Chamber is once more aware that at this moment there is no holiday for you. I, nevertheless, wish that during the coming three weeks you'll have an opportunity perhaps to relax, perhaps to do a few more things than you usually can do even in a detention situation. That's what the Chamber wishes you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to thank you for that, and I would like to wish you a very pleasant holiday and to everyone else too. And at least my family might be able to visit me and I will benefit from this holiday in this way, and I will take that opportunity to have a rest. And I wish everyone a very good holiday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your words and I'm happy at least that you can receive a visit from your family and do a few things you would not be able to do otherwise. We will then adjourn. A scheduling order will tell us when further hearings will take place. And it's expected therefore, that the 7th of October, the Defence, unless of course, a motion not yet been filed, would be granted, should start the presentation of its case. The Court adjourns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2.12 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday the 7th day of October, 2002, at a time to be determined. 20 21 22 23 24 25
